Drug-Free Workplace Policy The Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) is committed to maintaining a safe, drug-free workplace. All DLA employees are required to refrain from illegal drug use on and off duty. DLA conducts pre-employment, reasonable suspicion, post-accident, and random drug testing. Applicants tentatively selected for employment in testing designated positions will undergo a urinalysis to screen for illegal drug use prior to appointment. Refusal to undergo testing or testing positive for illegal drugs will result in withdrawal of the tentative job offer and a six-month denial of employment with DLA from the date of the drug test. Employees in drug testing designated positions are subject to random drug testing. A negative drug test result must be received by HR within 30 calendar days after the EOD (i.e., start date). The selectee's inability successfully pass; or refusal to conduct the test may result in: 1) the tentative or FJO being withdrawn during the recruitment process; or 2) subsequently being removed from Federal service for failure to meet a condition of employment. You may be required to sign a "Drug Test Statement of Understanding" if you are selected for this position. The DLA drug testing panel tests for the following substances: marijuana, cocaine, opiates, heroin, phencyclidine, amphetamines, methamphetamines, fentanyl, norfentanyl, methylenedioxymethamphetamine (MDMA), methylenedioxyamphetamine (MDA), and opioids. ADVISORY: Use of cannabidiol (CBD) products may result in a positive drug test for marijuana. DLA employees are subject to Federal law and under Federal law, Marijuana is illegal. MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Experience requirements are described in the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualification Standards for General Schedule Positions, Administrative and Management Positions. SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE: Applicants must have at least 1 year (52 weeks) of specialized experience at the next lower broadband NH-03, equivalent to the next lower grade GS-13 or equivalent in other pay systems. Specialized experience is experience in applying a mastery of security policies, IT principles, and safety regulations to acquisition and logistics supportability disciplines to solve complex security issues. Proficiency in directing organizational staff and serving as a Government Special Security Officer (GSSO) for MAJCOM Special Access Programs (SAP), leading security inspections, and providing expert oversight to senior leadership. Expertise also includes applying comprehensive knowledge of Intelligence Community (IC) and IJSTO directives to manage Top Secret Sensitive Compartmented Information Facilities (SCIFs) and specialized security networks, while utilizing strong communication skills to prepare and present high-level documentation and briefings. NOTE: Due to the use of 120-day rosters, this period of experience may be completed within 120 days of the closing date of this announcement. KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES (KSAs): Your qualifications will be evaluated on the basis of your level of knowledge, skills, abilities and/or competencies in the following areas: Mastery knowledge of security policies, procedures, and practices related to the acquisition and logistics supportability disciplines, their interrelationships, resources and applicability to the mission of AFMC. Extensive knowledge of a wide range of IT principles, concepts, and methods. Knowledge of safety and security regulations, practices, and procedures. Ability to plan, organize, and direct the functions and staff of a small to medium sized organization. Demonstrated skill in both oral and written communications for the purpose of effectively preparing and/or presenting a diverse array of documentation and other materials. Comprehensive knowledge of the Intelligence Community (IC) and Integrated Joint Special Technical Operations (IJSTO) directives applicable to the establishment and management of Top Secret Sensitive Compartmented Information Facilities. Thorough knowledge of special program and specialized management of the government security network to respond to and solve varied and complex security issues with sensitive situations. PART-TIME OR UNPAID EXPERIENCE: Credit will be given for appropriate unpaid and or part-time work. You must clearly identify the duties and responsibilities in each position held and the total number of hours per week. VOLUNTEER WORK EXPERIENCE: Refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service Programs (i.e., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student and social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge and skills that can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment.You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

Details.JobSummary: About the position: This position is Non-appropriated Fund (NAF) and is located at the NAF Human Resources Office, Yokota AB. This is Regular Full-Time Position, guaranteed 40 hours a week.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Thank you for considering employment with Air Force Services Non-Appropriated Funds (NAF). The 374 Force Support Squadron is a team of 1,000+ military, civilians and local nationals. We work together to provide enhanced quality of life for the 12,000 Yokota Air Base community members and over 150,000 transient personnel that visit Yokota every year via facilities and programs centered on morale, welfare, recreation and total force development. Our operations are the fourth largest in the Air Force: 13 dining facilities; personnel readiness and accountability; lodging; fitness; recreation; resiliency; child and youth programs; community building; mortuary affairs; NEO; Professional Development; and Education and Training. The squadron is comprised of eight flights, 49 activities and 159 facilities.
MajorDuties: Serves as the subject matter expert and primary point-of-contact on all administrative, procedural, and regulatory requirements for the Yokota AB NAF Human Resources Security Program. Responsible for ensuring all security and background investigation requirements are in compliance with current directives for all NAF new hires, current employees, FSS volunteers, instructors, FCC providers, and any other individual associated with the FSS. Processes and tracks all levels of background investigations (Tier 1, Tier 2, etc), Installation Records Checks (IRCs) for current and previous installations, Special Agreement Checks (SACs), and all associated and incidental paperwork in accordance with position requirements. Complies with incoming IRC requests within the specified time-lines as necessary. Enforces accountability time-lines for NAF new-hires to ensure strict adherence to background investigation regulatory compliance. Effectively maintains current excel/database trackers reflecting the current status of all FSS investigations. Utilizes Electronic Questionnaires for Investigations Processing (e-QIP), Joint Personnel Adjudication System (JPAS), and other related systems to initiate, inquire about, and close investigations. Troubleshoots when appropriate, and remedies delays by working with the 374 AW/IPO and related agencies as needed. Routinely and in a timely manner, mails investigative documents to the Office of Personnel Management (OPM). Serves as the primary focal point to receive and respond to written and verbal inquiries from the Installation Protection Office (IPO), Department of Defense Central Adjudications Facility (DoDCAF), and OPM. Serves as the liaison between these offices, employees, and supervisors to provide accurate information, clarification, or remedy any issues. Screens for suitability issues on applications and background investigations. Refers suitability issues to agency adjudication officers for further review and adjudication. Establishes and maintains background investigative files and properly stages investigative documents as required. Properly disposes of background investigative files according to records management directives. May be required to research and download forms and publications related to investigative requirements. Posts updates to directives and stays up-to-date on all changes to investigatory requirements as they occur. Updates the Defense Civilian Personnel Data System (DCPDS) to reflect completion of investigatory requirements. Prints form NAF-17 and files in the Official Personnel File (OPF) reflecting updated information. Maintains current continuity binder reflecting the current processes and succession planning information. Conducts fingerprinting as required. Reports security processing timeliness at least quarterly. When not performing security duties, will assist with the completion of Human Resources Assistant duties. Performs other related duties as assigned. If interested in this position please preview the online application: https://apply.usastaffing.gov/ViewQuestionnaire/13102244
